title: Quant SlabBench: integrated ops harness for quantization trade-off surfacing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a reproducible, operations-friendly benchmarking harness ("SlabBench") that evaluates quantization configurations (FP16 / INT8 / INT4) across representative production workloads and surfaces the quality/performance frontier to engineering and product teams.

Context: Existing quantization sweeps have focused on single-model runs or isolated latency measurements. For customers and platform owners we need: (1) steady-state tokens/sec under realistic concurrency, (2) p95 latency under target SLO shapes, (3) regression detection for generation quality (perplexity/ROUGE/LLM-eval sets), and (4) deterministic artifacts that can be ingested by console and alerting.

Success criteria: harness runs end-to-end with automated setup, produces time-series metrics (tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency), quality deltas per prompt set, and a compact CSV + Grafana dashboard link. Regression detector should flag >2% quality drop or >10% tokens/sec improvement degradation compared to baseline and file an automatic regression alert ticket.

Scope/Non-goals: does not include model training or new quant kernels. Focus is on orchestration, load shaping, sampling strategy, and signal extraction for FP16/INT8/INT4 artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: SlabBench can run a 1-hour sweep across FP16/INT8/INT4 for a target model on a dedicated GPU instance and produce reproducible CSV artifact.
Metrics emitted to Prometheus compatible metrics sink with tokens_per_sec, inferences, p50/p95/p99_latency, and quality_score for each quant profile and sequence-length bucket.
Automatic regression detection runs at the end of each sweep and opens ENG- tickets when thresholds are breached, with a human-review flag.
Dashboard (Grafana) panel template is created and linked in results_artifacts for cross-team review.
Harness integrates with existing perf infra (bench-runner service) and reuses KV-caching shim to simulate warm cache conditions.
tasks: Design workload mix (short/medium/long sequence buckets) and sampling strategy for representative production traffic
Implement orchestration runner that parallelizes quant variants and captures token-level traces
Add exporter to metrics pipeline for tokens/sec and p95 by variant and seq-bucket
Implement quality evaluation step (LLM-eval promptset + delta calculation) and normalize scores to baseline
Add statistical regression detector (CUSUM/control-chart) and policy to create tickets when triggered
Create Grafana dashboard template and testing checklist
Wire S3/drive artifact upload with versioned CSV naming and retention policy
Write runbook for on-call when a sweep triggers a regression alert
notes: Design decision: use interleaved-run strategy (rotate quant variants every 30s) to minimize temporal drift between variants and strengthen comparative signal.
Trade-off: interleaving increases GPU context-switching vs. isolated long runs; chosen because it reduces confounding from host load variability.
Quality metrics: primary is normalized LLM-eval pass@k delta and embedding-similarity AUC for semantic drift. Perplexity used as auxiliary signal for generation models.
Latency measurement: measure end-to-end latency including serialization and network hop simulated by local proxy to reflect hosted API stack.
We will bucket tokens/sec and latency by sequence-length buckets: short (<64), medium (64-512), long (>512).
Regression thresholds: quality_delta <= -2% OR p95_latency_increase >= +15% OR tokens_per_sec decrease >= 10% triggers alert. Thresholds are conservative and will be tuned after first 5 runs.
